role: author paraphrases of opened original sources, not independent verification

sources.attribution: DEX 2009 and older dictionary entries, first physical sense; DOOM/DOR paradigm
sources.paraphrase: Fine particles suspended in air or deposited on surfaces. The mass-noun dust sense is distinct from qualified powders and medicinal plurals. Only praful/prafului are proposed; prafuri, pulbere, colb and broad synonyms are held.

A small piece detached from bread, generalized to tiny pieces of food. Firimituri, firimiturile, firimiturii and firimiturilor are ordinary forms. Firimitura already normalizes to the label; no redundant stored form. Firmitură is a dictionary variant but excluded from this wave.

sources.attribution: DEX 2009/1998 first textile sense and DOOM forms
sources.paraphrase: Scamă is a short thread detached from fabric. Scame, scamele, scamei and scamelor preserve that owner. The plural botanical sense is secondary and not modeled; hair, dust, fluff and broad fibre are not synonyms.
A household shovel-shaped object gathers sweepings from a broom. Establishes long-standing Romanian familiarity and the object rather than the idiom. This alone does not establish Contexto C3.

sources.attribution: DEX 2009; historical definitions on the parent page
sources.paraphrase: A device for sucking up dust and other substances. Household owner is already explicitly scoped by the KG description. Electricity is established by manufacturer specifications, not this general dictionary definition.
A plate is a food-serving vessel. Together with manufacturer guidance covering dishes, this supports a qualified manual-washing link; it does not imply abrasive sponges are safe for every plate.

sources.attribution: Leifheit Romanian dry-cleaning category and broom/dustpan products
sources.paraphrase: The original brand page discusses floor dust, hair and crumbs alongside hand/long-handle brush sets and broom/dustpan sets. Proposed dust/crumb collection links refer to dry sweepings from floors, not all industrial dust or edible processing.
Manufacturer describes microfiber fringes collecting dust from floors. The edge is qualified to a microfiber mop and does not claim every mop is used dry.

sources.attribution: Kärcher Romanian vacuum family and dust composition explanation
sources.paraphrase: The page presents cordless battery-powered vacuums and describes dust as a mixture including carpet fibres. Supports household dust collection, battery electrical operation and a qualified carpet contribution to household dust. It does not equate dust with soil or lint.

The original carpet-care text explicitly identifies biscuit crumbs among routine floor soilings and recommends regular vacuum cleaning, including rapid cordless vacuum use. Links concern ordinary dry crumb collection; water is not claimed necessary for vacuuming.

sources.attribution: Kärcher original VC-series manual, Romanian section
sources.paraphrase: Romanian instructions identify connecting the power plug to the outlet, circuit breakers and adjustable power for floors/carpets. Together with the cordless family page, supports electricity from the mains or battery as operating energy.

sources.attribution: Philips original Romanian GCA2100 fabric-shaver page
sources.paraphrase: Names clothes and blankets as textiles carrying removable lint. Alongside the dictionary definition, supports qualified may-shed links for Haină and Pătură. No extra Pulover node is proposed just because it appears in the source.

sources.attribution: IKEA of Sweden original Romanian wool-rug care instructions
sources.paraphrase: The manufacturer says wool rugs shed lint naturally and recommends regular vacuuming. Supports a qualified may-shed edge for some carpets, especially wool, and lint/carpet removal with a vacuum; not all carpet materials are asserted to shed identically.

sources.attribution: Kärcher original Romanian robot vacuum family
sources.paraphrase: Describes vacuum power removing dust and lint from hard floors and short-pile carpets. Proposed lint-to-vacuum link is about loose debris on those surfaces; it does not claim a floor vacuum replaces a fabric shaver for attached clothing pills.

sources.attribution: FINO original Romanian kitchen-sponge product and care guidance
sources.paraphrase: Kitchen sponges wash utensils and dishes; rinse and drain after use. It cautions about abrasive sides on delicate/nonstick surfaces. With the food-serving plate definition, supports Farfurie→Burete de vase and water for wetting/rinsing.

sources.attribution: Vileda original Romanian Glitzi PUR Active guidance
sources.paraphrase: The manufacturer explicitly discusses washing and reusing the sponge with water and soap. Supports water used with a dish sponge; not a water-only cleaning recipe.

sources.attribution: Romanian brand owner epack original product inventory
sources.paraphrase: Current range of ordinary dish sponges including foam and cellulose provides a second manufacturer recognition signal for Burete de vase. Raw target approval still needs actual C1–C6 judgments.

The historical definition includes absorbent washing objects manufactured from rubber or plastic, separate from fungi and marine organisms. Current dish-sponge manufacturers establish the specifically qualified Burete de vase sense; the broad word burete is not added as an alias.

strength_policy: All 0.70–0.90 strengths are explicit editorial estimates of association directness, not numbers measured by a source. All 17 edges are one-way; reverse traversability is not inferred.
unresolved: DEX farfurie canonical open returned a transient error; the dictionary entry URL above returned the original DEX wording in search.
DEX aspirator does not explicitly establish electrical operation. Its edge proof relies on the original manual and cordless-vacuum specifications.
